item.content:encoded:
Whether you want to explore new feature sets, dissect the architecture of our event infrastructure, or challenge your skills, here is your playbook for the Hands-on Labs at Explore this year.

REGISTER NOW

Written By: Kelly Smith, Product Marketing Engineer, VMware Hands-on Labs

As a virtual infrastructure or cloud administrator, you spend your days managing environments, keeping up with change, and evaluating where your private cloud strategy is heading next. The best way to master new capabilities isn’t watching a passive demo—it’s logging directly into a live console and driving the software yourself with expert guidance nearby.

That is why the Hands-on Labs room is the ultimate destination for technical administrators and engineers at Explore. This is where you get exclusive, first-look access to our brand-new VCF 9.1 lab content. While VCF 9.1 went GA earlier this summer, Explore is the official in-person debut of the lab environments built specifically around it.

1. The Heavy Hitters: 36 Expert-led Workshops

Think of our Expert-led Workshops as highly technical, interactive deep dives led directly by the specialists who live and breathe this technology in the field every day.

  • Admin Access: These workshops bypass passive observation and place you directly inside a live, fully-functioning sandbox environment with admin rights.
  • Direct Line to Field Experts: These 36 workshops are developed and presented by the actual Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) who built the labs. They work directly with customers in the field daily, giving you a direct line to ask practical, real-world questions about architecture, migration, automation, or security.
  • Deep Technical Variety: This year’s catalog covers the critical fronts of modern infrastructure management, including:
    • Core Cloud Operations: Day 2 diagnostics, health triage, and performance tuning (like vNUMA and processor optimization).
    • Advanced Networking & Storage: Multi-site BGP peering, native VPC routing, and advanced Elastic Storage Architecture (ESA).
    • Automation & Next-Gen Workloads: Infrastructure-as-code deployments with Salt, workload mobility with HCX, and even building your first Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) app with private AI.
  • The Standby Hack: Because these sessions offer such high-value technical depth, they fill up instantly in the catalog. If a workshop you need is marked as full, show up to the room anyway. Standby seats are available onsite for walk-in practitioners to cover last-minute no-shows.

2. Learn at Your Own Pace: Over 30 Self-paced Labs

Need to break away from a rigid schedule, or want to dive deep into a specific VCF 9.1 configuration on your own time?

  • 30+ Interactive Lab Titles: Our Self-paced Labs catalog features over 30 unique, interactive titles covering the entire portfolio. There is no pre-registration or scheduling required—just walk in, grab an open station, and start learning.
  • SMEs on Standby: Just because it’s a Self-paced Lab doesn’t mean you’re learning in isolation. Our product SMEs are stationed right on the floor. If you hit an interesting scenario, have a question about a new 9.1 feature, or want to know how a lab configuration translates to your real-world environment, just raise your hand.

3. Peak “Software on Software”: The Hands-on Labs Tour & Command Center

Ever wondered what it takes to spin up, monitor, and tear down thousands of highly concurrent, live nested lab environments for an event of this scale? We do it by running our own software stack at absolute peak capacity.

  • The 12-Screen Command Center Wall: See the real-time performance, compute, storage, and networking metrics of the entire Hands-on Labs event space in real time. This is a true, live showcase of the platform operating under extreme real-world pressure.
  • Go Behind the Scenes: Join our infrastructure admins, performance teams, and lab builders for the Hands-on Labs Tour of our deployment architecture. We’ll talk capacity planning, automation, and how we handle the massive workloads generated by thousands of concurrent users.
  • Deep Dive Ahead: Want a sneak peek at the infrastructure and business logic that powers this massive operation? Read our dedicated Hands-on Labs Tour blog post here for the full architectural breakdown.

4. Challenge Your Skills: Odyssey & The VCF Lab Explorer’s Tracker 

We know that technical admins love a friendly challenge and a bit of bragging rights. We have built-in opportunities to do both.

  • The Odyssey Tournament: Think you’re the fastest admin in the room? Put your troubleshooting and configuration skills to the test in our gamified live-lab tournament. Race against your peers to solve real-world technical challenges, climb the live leaderboard, and walk away with major prizes and ultimate bragging rights. Details on the challenge and prizes in this blog post.
  • VCF Lab Explorer Tracker: Start your journey by visiting the VCF demo booth on the show floor to grab your VCF Keychain. From there, head over to the Hands-on Labs area, complete specific technical milestones, and collect exclusive charms to add to your keychain. Completing your passport unlocks a custom plushie and enters you for a chance to win a highly coveted, limited-edition VCF sweatshirt.

Lock In Your Schedule

The Hands-on Labs room is where you stop watching demos and start actually using the new technology.

  • Browse the catalog and reserve your Expert-led Workshop seats now
  • Read our deep-dive on the Hands-on Labs Command Center
  • Learn more about the Hands-on Labs Tour
  • Get all the details on Odyssey rules, times, and prizes
REGISTER NOW

Stay connected with VMware Hands-on Labs on X, Facebook, and YouTube.

Are you a fan of hands-on learning? Check out this ultimate guide for Hands-on Labs at #VMwareExplore 2026 in Las Vegas!
Share on X

item.content:encoded:
VMware Explore is the perfect career stepping stone. Take advantage of every moment onsite to gain hands-on experience and validate your expertise. 

Here are the top learning and certification opportunities you can’t afford to miss in Las Vegas.

Must-See Session: Distributed Security

Traditional perimeter security creates blind spots in East-West traffic that dynamic workloads can’t afford. Join Tim Burkard (v/Gandalf) and Chris McCain for Demystifying VMware vDefend Distributed Security Within VMware Cloud Foundation to see how Broadcom is reimagining protection.

In this essential session, you’ll discover how VMware vDefend closes security gaps by embedding firewalling, threat detection, and microsegmentation directly into the virtualization layer. Learn to eliminate blind spots, simplify complex operations, and safeguard your most critical workloads using proven, AI-driven strategies.

Don’t miss this chance to master the Distributed Firewall and Intrusion Protection systems within your network stack. Schedule now to secure your spot at this session and level up your private cloud security posture.

Get Certified at the Certification Exam Center 

Planning on getting VMware certified? Why wait? There’s no better time or place to make this strategic career investment.

  • Exclusive Savings: Full Event Pass holders receive one complimentary VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) certification voucher (VCP or VCAP level), making it easier than ever to validate your skills.
  • Onsite Convenience: Test without leaving the venue at the Certification Exam Center (Lido Ballroom 3005, Level 3).
  • Professional Momentum: Sharpen your knowledge right before sitting for your exam with onsite breakout sessions, prep labs, and expert Q&A.

Need guidance? Our team of VCF Learning specialists will be stationed at the Lido Ballroom registration desk all week to answer questions and help you chart your path.

Why Being Certified in Private Cloud Is More Important Than Ever

As organizations accelerate their adoption of VCF to power their hybrid and AI-ready data centers, the demand for private cloud expertise is growing. Employers are looking for specialists who can architect, automate, and manage a private cloud at enterprise scale.

VCF certification is more than a credential. It proves to the industry that you have the deep skills needed to design and operate modern infrastructure in the AI era. Training and certification give you expertise that positions you as an indispensable leader in your organization.

VMware Certified Advanced Professional (VCAP)

The new VCAP-VCF certifications elevate your profile and act as catalysts for significant professional growth. These credentials verify your ability to architect and operate VMware Cloud Foundation environments at enterprise scale. Moving beyond fundamental knowledge, the VCAP proves you possess the strategic expertise to lead complex private cloud initiatives and deliver high-impact results. 

Elevate Your Expertise with VCAP Exams

Explore 2026 offers the perfect opportunity to validate your advanced skills with our new VMware Certified Advanced Professional (VCAP) certifications in VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF). Currently available exams include VCAP-VCF: VKS, Automation, Operations, Networking, Storage.

To further assist you, our team of VCF Learning specialists will be available at the Certification Exam Center registration area all week to offer guidance and answer any questions you may have.

VMware Explore Attendees, This Is for You!

Want to get ahead of the curve and score an exclusive surprise swag? Be among the first to earn your VCAP-VCF certification. This offer is strictly for VMware Explore attendees and only available onsite while supplies last—don’t miss your chance.

Earning your certification in Las Vegas is the fastest way to validate your skills, return home ready to lead enterprise strategy, and level up your career.

  • Already have your Full Event Pass? Check your inbox for your unique exam scheduling instructions.
  • Haven’t registered yet? Register for VMware Explore 2026 today.

item.title: Headlamp as a VMware vSphere Kubernetes Service Add-on
item.dc:creator: vmwareblogs
item.description:
For years, the Kubernetes Dashboard project provided a web UI to manage and monitor a Kubernetes cluster and applications. This made it easy for platform engineers to troubleshoot issues. However, the Kubernetes project officially deprecated and archived the Kubernetes Dashboard in early 2026. Since then, the focus has shifted to Headlamp as the recommended alternative. … Continued

The post Headlamp as a VMware vSphere Kubernetes Service Add-on appeared first on VMware Blogs.
item.content:encoded:
For years, the Kubernetes Dashboard project provided a web UI to manage and monitor a Kubernetes cluster and applications. This made it easy for platform engineers to troubleshoot issues. However, the Kubernetes project officially deprecated and archived the Kubernetes Dashboard in early 2026. Since then, the focus has shifted to Headlamp as the recommended alternative.

Kubernetes Dashboard (deprecated)

Teams running VMware vSphere Kubernetes Service (VKS) on VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) have strong monitoring options. In fact, VCF Operations already provides the capability to monitor VKS cluster health alongside the broader virtualization estate. Specifically, it gives platform administrators a single pane of glass across VMs and Kubernetes clusters. For instance, they can monitor node utilization, capacity planning, cost visibility, and macro-level health. 

VKS monitoring in VCF Operations

Overall, VCF Operations excels at this platform-wide operational view. However, platform engineers and Site Reliability Engineers (SREs) often need to focus on one specific cluster. In particular, they need deeper application details to manage and troubleshoot applications. For example, day-to-day workflow requires moment-to-moment interaction with specific workloads like viewing live container logs, investigating a crash-looping pod, executing into a shell, or adjusting a ConfigMap on the fly.

This is where Headlamp comes in. Headlamp provides a governed, RBAC-aware UI for the Kubernetes cluster and applications running on it. 

Infrastructure administrators rely on VCF Operations to ensure the platform is healthy and optimized, while platform engineers use Headlamp as an in-cluster tool that respects their Kubernetes permissions and eliminates the need to view the entire infrastructure estate. In other words, the two tools are complementary by design.

Introduction to Headlamp: a Kubernetes UI built for extensibility

Headlamp is a CNCF Sandbox project that provides an open-source, extensible Kubernetes web UI. It combines the resource visibility you expect from any dashboard, such as workload status, logs, and exec access. It also includes a plugin architecture that lets platform teams add purpose-built views.

Headlamp UI

What problems does Headlamp solve?

The Kubernetes project has now deprecated and archived the Kubernetes Dashboard. Teams that relied on it for day-to-day visibility need an actively maintained replacement built for modern cluster scale. Kubectl works well for operators comfortable with complex queries, but it hits a wall when broader platform engineer adoption is needed. Headlamp addresses three concrete pain points for Kubernetes environments.

To begin with, it gives platform engineers read-write access through a governed, role-aware interface. As a result, the UI controls surface based on the authenticated user’s permissions. Thus, teams can safely open cluster access to platform engineers without risking accidental destructive operations. 

Furthermore, it replaces the context-switching burden of jumping between terminals, dashboards, and documentation tabs. For instance, Headlamp bundles a log viewer, an in-browser shell, a YAML editor with inline documentation, and a resource map into a single application. 

Finally, it provides a stable surface for extending operational workflows through plugins. Rather than building a separate internal tool every time a new capability is needed, such as cert-manager certificate health, the Headlamp plugin system lets teams embed those views directly into the existing UI.

The value of Headlamp VKS add-on for platform teams

VMware vSphere Kubernetes Service on VCF 9.1 delivers CNCF-certified Kubernetes clusters provisioned through Cluster API, backed by vSphere High Availability (HA) and Distributed Resource Scheduler (DRS), and managed through a declarative add-on framework. That infrastructure foundation gives platform teams a reliable, enterprise-grade substrate. Headlamp complements it by providing the human interface layer on top of that substrate.

Headlamp has been introduced as an Ecosystem Tier Add-On in VKS 3.7. Release notes for VKS 3.7 can be found here.

Plugin extensibility within the VCF ecosystem

The VKS Add-on framework already extends the base Kubernetes feature set with validated, lifecycle-managed software components. Headlamp is classified as an Ecosystem Tier package which means Broadcom supports the lifecycle management of the add-on (thus reducing the operational burden of keeping Headlamp updated compared to managing it as a standalone open-source project) while leveraging the expert-led power of the global community for runtime support.

The Headlamp add-on released with VKS 3.7 supports automatic plugin installation in Headlamp for cert-manager and prometheus if the cert-manager or prometheus add-ons are installed on the VKS cluster. Even if you install these add-ons after you install Headlamp, the add-on controller continuously checks for the installation of these add-ons and is able to install the plugin in Headlamp.

Headlamp Plugins

Deploying Headlamp as an add-on in VKS

Let’s walk through a complete deployment together, from prerequisites to a working UI endpoint. 

Prerequisites

Before proceeding, ensure the following conditions are met in your environment.

  1. VKS 3.7 enabled on the Supervisor
  2. Cert-Manager add-on installed on the VKS cluster

Supervisor enabled with VKS 3.7

Deployment Steps

For this demonstration, we’ve already created a test namespace in VCF Automation and deployed a VKS 3.7 (Kubernetes 1.36) cluster in VCF 9.1. 

VKS 3.7 cluster in VCF Automation

You need this setup to follow along and use the VKS Cluster Management tab in VCF Automation for add-on management that we will showcase in this blog. However, if the VKS cluster is created outside a VCF Automation namespace (for example, using Local Consumption Interface (LCI) in VMware vCenter), then you can follow the steps outlined in the VCF documentation to achieve the same through CLI commands.

  1. Log in to the VCF Automation Organization portal and click on Manage & Govern > Kubernetes Management > Clusters and click on the VKS cluster.

VKS Cluster Management

  1. Then, navigate to the Add-ons tab > Repositories and you should see the VKS 3.7 add-on repository available once you enable VKS 3.7 on Supervisor.

VKS Add-on repository

  1. Then, navigate to Available Add-ons and look for the Headlamp add-on.

Available Add-on list

  1. Click on Install Add-On.

Headlamp Add-On deployment

  1. Then, provide a name for the package, select the version you want to deploy, and click on Install Add-On.

Headlamp Add-On installation

The add-on installs fairly quickly.

Headlamp Add-On verification

Retrieving the external IP address

Once the add-on is installed, we need to get the external IP address assigned to headlamp to access its UI. One option is to navigate to Build & Deploy > test namespace > Network > Services and search for headlamp in the filter tab. The service gets annotated with a label “run.tanzu.vmware.com/service.name: headlamp” that makes it easy to find.

Headlamp verification – External IP

The other option to get the external IP is to use the kubectl command to get the IP from the VKS cluster by using the command:

Headlamp verification – kubectl output

Accessing the Headlamp UI

Once we have the external IP, we can access its UI via a web browser. Headlamp also supports OIDC integration, meaning users can integrate their existing Identity Providers with Headlamp to provide RBAC with Headlamp using their existing systems.

Headlamp Authentication UI

Generating an authentication token

Now, we need to generate an authentication token to access the VKS cluster. This ensures RBAC is maintained and the correct level of permissions are available on the cluster within headlamp as the end-user has access to. To generate the auth token, we go back to the CLI with VKS cluster access and create a ClusterRoleBinding and generate a token (the best practice is to generate a RoleBinding or ClusterRoleBinding with the least privilege required to perform the set of actions required):

Headlamp auth token generation

Verifying cluster access

Once you take this auth token and paste it in the Headlamp UI, you will be able to access the VKS cluster details:

Headlamp UI with cluster details

Headlamp UI – Map view

Now an SRE or platform engineer has access to this specific VKS cluster and can manage the cluster and the applications deployed in it using the Headlamp UI.

Summary

In summary, the Headlamp add-on is straightforward and very quick to install and integrates with OIDC identity providers already present in most VCF environments.

If your VKS environment is running on VKS 3.7 and Headlamp is not yet part of your add-on stack, the deployment guide above gives you everything needed to stand up a production-grade instance today.

item.content:encoded:
Get ready for VMware Explore Las Vegas, August 31 – September 3, 2026. We’ve put together an exceptional lineup of VCF Edge sessions at VMware Explore Las Vegas designed to deliver immediate, real-world value.

Today, edge computing and artificial intelligence (AI) are no longer afterthoughts; they are the critical twin pillars of modern enterprise IT. As data generation at the edge accelerates, combining robust edge infrastructure with intelligent AI workloads is essential for driving real-time automation and autonomous decision-making. To help you navigate this fast-moving landscape, we’ve built a strong lineup of breakout sessions designed to deliver immediate, real-world value you can put to work right away. Explore our curated guide below to discover the top VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) Edge sessions, and start scheduling them in the content catalog today. 

Key VMware Cloud Foundation at the Edge Breakout Sessions

AI at the Edge: Running Inference and Agentic Workflows with VCF Edge

CLOB1272LV | Monday, Aug 31 | 9:00 AM – 9:45 AM PDT

Industries adopting agentic workflows to automate edge operations require reliable, scalable AI infrastructure with standardized orchestration for production deployment. This session addresses three critical edge AI constraints: 

  • Sub-10ms inference latency for closed-loop control systems
  • Local sensor processing to eliminate network backhaul 
  • Data residency compliance in regulated environments 

We examine the VCF Edge AI stack: vGPU resource partitioning strategies, vLLM runtime automation for model deployment and versioning, and access controls for AI governance. Attendees learn reference architectures for deploying high-availability computer vision pipelines and agentic workflows across distributed edge fleets with centralized management. 

Deploy with Confidence: Tactical and Government Edge Architectures

CLOB1831LV | Monday, Aug 31 | 10:15 AM – 11:00 AM PDT

Government agencies operate across a vast spectrum, from connected enterprise campuses to austere tactical edges with severe power, space, and staffing constraints. Choosing the right architecture requires balancing workloads with strict operational realities. In this session, experts break down deployment models within VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) Edge. 

From single-node, remote deployments to multi-host configurations at major agency sites, we provide a practical framework to map mission requirements to the right architecture. What you will learn: 

  • How to evaluate connectivity, footprint, and compliance across VCF Edge models
  •  Best practices for matching traditional VMs and containerized workloads to the right deployment scale 
  • How architectural consistency simplifies Day 2 operations and scaling 

VMware vSphere Kubernetes Service (VKS) at the Edge: Production Design and Architecture Best Practices

CLOB1146LV | Tuesday, September 1 | 9:00 AM – 9:45 AM PDT

Deploying Kubernetes at the edge introduces unique challenges: resource sizing; scaling to a large number of locations; limited bandwidth; high latency; and managing connectivity loss. This session explores best practices for designing and deploying VMware vSphere Kubernetes Service (VKS) on VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) to support production edge workloads. Attendees will learn how to architect small-footprint clusters, design connectivity between central and edge locations, and enable resilient operations in low/no-connectivity scenarios. 

We will cover GitOps-driven deployment using Argo CD, local image management with Harbor, and strategies for maintaining consistency across distributed sites. You will leave with a framework to deploy and operate modern workloads at the edge with confidence, ensuring scalability, reliability, and operational simplicity. 

VMware Cloud Foundation Edge 9.1: A Purpose-Built Platform for the Distributed Edge

CLOB1175LV | Tuesday, September 1 | 3:00 PM – 3:45 PM PDT

The edge is the new frontier of the modern private cloud, but managing distributed sites with zero local IT staff presents massive operational challenges. This session introduces the latest innovations in VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) Edge 9.1, a lightweight architecture with options for the unique demands of retail, manufacturing, and defense. New capabilities streamline rollout of infrastructure and slash deployment times for workloads. 

We will explore how new Live Patching capabilities help eliminate downtime and how the platform secures distributed environments through confidential computing. Whether you are scaling edge AI workloads or navigating strict HIPAA and PCI compliance, you will walk away with a blueprint for a self-healing, automated infrastructure that thrives where traditional data centers cannot. 

Living on the Edge: What’s New with VCF Edge

CLOB1260LV | Wednesday, Sept 2 | 9:00 AM – 9:45 AM PDT

We saved the big picture for Wednesday. This session brings together expert analysis on Edge Compute Trends from industry analyst David Linthicum as well as a detailed look at the latest innovations delivered in VCF Edge 9.1.

In this session, you’ll get an assessment of the key drivers of distributed edge infrastructure and how AI is reshaping the convergence of IT and OT.  Through customer case studies, this session will also highlight the key use cases and benefits of extending private cloud beyond the confines of the data center.  Whether you are still building a business case internally, or planning to scale your edge compute infrastructure globally, this is a must-attend session. 

Don’t Miss Us on the Show Floor

Stop by the VCF booth for a demo on “Deliver Scalable Autonomous Edge Architectures.” Our team will be running demos throughout the show, and it’s the best place ask product questions directly, and dig into use cases specific to your environment.

Start Planning Now

This year’s event brings together the technology and expertise you need to take AI beyond the traditional data center. Whether you’re building your edge AI roadmap, deploying intelligence directly at remote sites, or learning how to process workloads closer to where data is generated, VMware Explore in Las Vegas is the place to be.

We’re heading to Explore with alot of momentum behind VCF Edge, and we want you to be part of the conversation. Here’s a quick orientation based on where you’re focused:

  • Building an edge AI roadmap? Start Monday morning with CLOB1272LV.
  • Navigating government or mission-critical and tactical edge deployments? Join CLOB1831LV on Monday morning.
  • Modernizing Kubernetes skills at the edge? Block Tuesday morning for CLOB1146LV.
  • Scaling distributed operations or reducing site visits? Make the VCF Edge 9.1 deep dive (CLOB1175LV) your anchor session on Tuesday afternoon.
  • Looking for big-picture strategy and real-world customer insights? Catch Living on the Edge (CLOB1260LV) on Wednesday morning.

Learn more:

VMware Cloud Foundation Edge

VMware Cloud Foundation

item.title: Introducing the VMware Bootstrap Registry Appliance: Air-Gapped Harbor Service in VMware Cloud Foundation 9.0
item.dc:creator: dhruv tyagi
item.description:
Deploying containerized workloads in air-gapped environments has always required careful orchestration, especially when the platform registry you want to use cannot install itself without images it does not yet have. Consequently, streamlining the deployment of Harbor as a Supervisor Service in air-gapped VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) environments has been a key area of focus for … Continued

The post Introducing the VMware Bootstrap Registry Appliance: Air-Gapped Harbor Service in VMware Cloud Foundation 9.0 appeared first on VMware Blogs.
item.content:encoded:
Deploying containerized workloads in air-gapped environments has always required careful orchestration, especially when the platform registry you want to use cannot install itself without images it does not yet have. Consequently, streamlining the deployment of Harbor as a Supervisor Service in air-gapped VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) environments has been a key area of focus for us. While community-supported solutions like third-party registries provided an effective bridge in the past, we are now pleased to offer an official VCF-supported solution designed specifically for this workflow.

With the General Availability of the VMware Bootstrap Registry Appliance, we now have an official, VCF-supported solution: a purpose-built OVA that gives VCF customers a clean, secure, and operationally well-defined path to bootstrapping Harbor as a Supervisor Service in air-gapped VCF 9.0 and vSphere 8.0 Update 3 environments.

What Is the VMware Bootstrap Registry Appliance?

The VMware Bootstrap Registry Appliance is a hardened virtual appliance distributed as an OVA. Additionally, it ships with an OCI-compliant Harbor registry running natively on Photon OS 5.0 and is designed to host the OCI images required to enable Harbor Supervisor Service (and Contour) on the vSphere Supervisor.

However, the appliance is not a general-purpose enterprise registry and is not intended to serve workloads in production. Instead, it is Registry 0 in the air-gapped deployment sequence, a temporary bootstrapping tool that hands off responsibility to Harbor Supervisor Service (Registry 1) once that service is healthy and operational.

To maintain architectural compliance and supportability, the deployment of the VMware Bootstrap Registry Appliance is governed by the following mandatory operational constraints:

  • Exclusive Bootstrap Purpose: The VMware Bootstrap Registry Appliance shall only be utilized to upload and host the OCI images necessary to enable Contour and Harbor Supervisor services on the Supervisor.
  • Prohibition of Secondary Roles: The appliance must not be utilized for any other purpose within the infrastructure. Specifically, it is explicitly prohibited from serving as a permanent platform registry or enterprise workload registry.
  • Version-Specific Deployment Constraint: The use of the VMware Bootstrap Registry Appliance is restricted to deployments prior to VCF 9.1. Starting with VCF 9.1, the Fleet Depot Service (FDS) serves as the officially supported solution for air-gapped environment lifecycle management.

Downloading the VMware Bootstrap Registry Appliance

The appliance is available on the Broadcom Support Portal at the following paths:

  • For vSphere 8.0:
    •  Broadcom Support Portal > My Downloads > VMware vSphere > VMware vSphere Standard > 8.0 > Drivers and Tools > VMware Bootstrap Appliance > BOOTSTRAP_APPLIANCE-2.15.2+vmware.1-25635995.ova
  • For VCF 9.0:
    • Broadcom Support Portal > My Downloads > VMware Cloud Foundation > VMware Cloud Foundation 9 – 9.0.2 > VMware vCenter > Drivers and Tools > VMware Bootstrap Appliance > BOOTSTRAP_APPLIANCE-2.15.2+vmware.1-25635995.ova

Deployment Overview

Air-gapped VCF deployments follow a two-phase approach. Initially, phase 1 establishes the bootstrap registry using the VMware Bootstrap Registry Appliance. Phase 2 deploys Harbor as a Supervisor Service, which then becomes the production registry for all workloads.

For a full step-by-step walkthrough including OVA deployment, Supervisor registration, image pre-staging with Carvel imgpkg and Harbor data values configuration required for air-gapped use, refer to the updated deployment blog: Deploying Harbor Service in Air-Gapped VMware Cloud Foundation 9.0 or the VMware vSphere Supervisor GitHub Repository.

Looking Ahead: VCF 9.1 and Fleet Depot Service

The VMware Bootstrap Registry Appliance is the right solution for VCF 9.0 and vSphere 8.0 U3 environments today. Customers upgrading to VCF 9.1 will benefit from the Fleet Depot Service (FDS). This built-in registry natively handles the bootstrapping lifecycle as part of the platform. In VCF 9.1 environments, you no longer need the VMware Bootstrap Registry Appliance, as FDS takes over this role.

Conclusion

In summary, the VMware Bootstrap Registry Appliance closes a gap in the air-gapped VCF deployment story. It offers a purpose-built, supported tool for bootstrapping the Harbor Supervisor Service. This replaces the Bitnami Harbor solution with a production-ready alternative. We recommend this path whether you are deploying fresh on VCF 9.0 or migrating an existing air-gapped environment.

Download the appliance from the Broadcom Support Portal under VMware vSphere or VCF 9.0, and follow the updated air-gapped Harbor deployment guide for the full step-by-step walkthrough. 

For more information on Harbor, follow our Harbor blog series:

  • Blog 1 – Harbor: Your Enterprise-Ready Container Registry for a Modern Private Cloud
  • Blog 2 – Reducing Harbor Deployment Complexity on Kubernetes
  • Blog 3 – Making Harbor Production-Ready: Essential Considerations for Deployment
  • Blog 4 – Integrating VMware Data Services Manager with Harbor for a Production-Ready Registry

item.dc:creator: chris wolf
item.description:
If you’ve been following the enterprise tech landscape this year, you already know what the most urgent conversation at VMware Explore 2026 in Las Vegas is going to be: AI. item.content:encoded:
If you’ve been following the enterprise tech landscape this year, you already know what the most urgent conversation at VMware Explore 2026 in Las Vegas is going to be: AI.

Over the past couple of years, AI has quickly evolved from pilot projects into an engine running daily business operations. Enterprise leaders everywhere are integrating LLMs and customized AI pipelines directly into business-critical workflows. But as AI moves into production, IT organizations need to balance high-performance GPU demands with strict data sovereignty and compliance requirements.

Agentic systems are the fastest-moving frontier in enterprise AI right now, and they come with a completely different infrastructure profile. Think about it: because these agents act almost like autonomous employees—constantly fetching, analyzing, and rewriting proprietary company data—they require strong access controls, traceability, and adaptive infrastructure that can meet their performance and scale requirements. 

Traditional AI deployment models simply weren’t designed for this. Sending autonomous, highly-privileged workloads to the public cloud triggers operational and compliance risks that hyperscalers often struggle to mitigate. What’s even more difficult is trying to provide consistent governance and policy enforcement across disparate silos for each AI cloud or PaaS the organization uses. 

The organizations that will win with AI in the next three years are the ones building sovereign, governed, production-grade AI infrastructure with control. VMware Cloud Foundation is that infrastructure, and Explore 2026 is where you learn how to build it.

Throughout the event, you’ll learn how to:

  • Build and run your AI agents and workflows: We’ll dive into how you can easily and securely leverage open-source software (OSS) alongside standards-based components and tooling.
  • Govern your  AI fleet: Discover how to ensure your AI agents and workloads can only access the data and execute the actions they are authorized for. We’ll be covering crucial topics like observability, cost and quota controls, policy enforcement, and sandboxing.
  • Protect against outside AI threats: As agents become more powerful, the threats will increasingly be AI-driven. We’ll show you how to lock down your environment and quickly recover from sophisticated AI-driven attacks.

To help you navigate the Explore content catalog, I’ve put together a curated list of my top picks for sessions on AI. I highly recommend building an agenda that addresses how to securely run multiple agents on a unified platform, without compromising on cost efficiency, performance, resiliency, or hardware choice.

My Top AI Session Picks for Las Vegas:

  • VMware Cloud Foundation Private AI Services: What’s New and What’s Next? [CLOB1661LV]
  • Business Impact of Agentic AI: A Customer Fireside Chat [CLOP1277LV]
  • Deploy and govern AI models and agents with VMware Cloud Foundation Private AI Services [CLOB1229LV]
  • Why Is VMware Cloud Foundation the Best Private Cloud Platform for Agentic AI Workloads? [CLOB1244LV]
  • Accelerating AI: Mastering GPU on VMware Cloud Foundation [INVB1237LV]
  • Powering Agentic AI: New Capabilities in VMware Cloud Foundation [VBT2044LV]

Hands-on Labs and Demos: Be sure to check out the AI-related HOLs (both expert-led workshops and self-paced labs) and demos available at Explore in Las Vegas.

Safe travels, and I look forward to seeing you in Las Vegas!

item.description:
官公庁や金融機関など、高度なセキュリティが求められる環境において、VMware vSphere® などのセキュリティ設定を評価し、担保することはインフラ運用の重要な課題です。本記事では、米国防総省（DoD）の基準であるDISA STIG（Security Technical Implementation Guide）を活用した、VMware プロダクトのセキュリティ監査、自動化、結果の可視化手法について解説します。 1. DISA STIG とは？ VMware との共同開発 STIGとは、米国防総省の情報システム局（DISA）が発行する、システムを安全に構成するための技術ガイドラインです。セキュリティ技術実装ガイド（STIG）は、国防情報システム局（DISA）が発行する構成標準であり、特定のソフトウェア製品が国防総省のセキュリティ要件を満たすためにどのように構成する必要があるかを規定しています。STIG は、構成すべき内容だけでなく、構成方法も定義しており、国防総省環境での使用が認められるためにシステムが満たすべき具体的な設定、値、検証手順などが含まれます。 STIG は、NIST SP 800-53 およびより広範な国防総省のセキュリティフレームワークから派生した一連のセキュリティ管理策を中心に構成されています。STIG 内の個々の要件は管理策（またはルール）と呼ばれ、各管理策には重大度評価（カテゴリI、II、III。それぞれ高、中、低の影響に対応）、セキュリティ設定の説明、準拠を確認する手順、および発見事項を是正する手順があります。   複数ベンダーが並ぶ DISA の STIG 管理サイト DISAの公式サイト（DoD Cyber Exchange）には、OS、データベース、ネットワーク機器からクラウドインフラに至るまで、多数のベンダー製品向けの STIG がラインナップされています。Microsoft®、Red Hat、Cisco®、VMware など、各ベンダー製品のセキュリティ基準がここで一元管理されています。 VMware と DISA の共同開発と最終承認 vSphere や VMware Cloud Foundation® 9 (VCF 9) 向けの STIG は、VMware と DISA が連携して共同開発しています。VMware が製品のアーキテクチャや最新機能（VCF の新機能など）に基づいたベストプラクティスを提案し、DISA … Continued

item.description:

item.content:encoded:
Running AI Agents as Governed Enterprise Infrastructure

The Challenge: Agentic AI Governance

AI agents have moved past answering questions. They call tools, query databases, run code, and hand work to other agents without a person in the loop. The controls that enterprises built for traditional software do not extend to this behavior. An API gateway has no concept of agent identity. It’s not usually clearly scoped in agentic AI, which tools an agent may call or which other agents it may reach. In most cases, it’s hard to understand what an agent did, under whose authority, and why.

The gap grows as agent deployments scale. An agent with open tool access inside the corporate network is a new attack surface, and the perimeter controls most organizations rely on were not built to close it. At the same time, inference spend across models and business units is difficult to measure and harder to cap. Before agents can move into production, they need three things that no single existing tool provides: verifiable identity, permissions bound by policy, and a complete audit trail. Regulated industries treat these as conditions of deployment, not enhancements.

The Solution

We are happy to announce the validation of Solo.io Enterprise for agentgateway and Solo.io Enterprise for kagent, on VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) by Broadcom and Solo.io. The validated solution gives agents these controls while keeping every model call, tool invocation, and policy decision inside the customer’s own infrastructure.

Solo.io Enterprise for agentgateway is an AI-native gateway that governs the traffic agents produce. Written in Rust and donated to the Agentic AI Foundation, it handles three classes of traffic from one control plane: LLM requests across on-premises and cloud models through a single endpoint, Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool access with per-tool authorization, and Agent-to-Agent (A2A) communication between services. It adds token-level cost attribution, budget enforcement, OAuth-based tool access, and audit trails, without the client changes a conventional proxy would require.

Solo.io Enterprise for kagent is the Kubernetes-native runtime for the agents themselves. Where agentgateway governs traffic to and between agents, kagent governs their identity, lifecycle, and behavior. Agents are declared as versioned Kubernetes resources, deployed through the same configuration workflows a platform team already runs, and tracked in Git. It ships with human-in-the-loop approval, policy management, and built-in agents for Kubernetes operations, Helm release management, and gateway administration. kagent is a CNCF Sandbox project with contributions from Google, Microsoft, IBM, and Amazon.

Together the two products supply what agents in production require: kagent gives each agent a managed identity and lifecycle, and agentgateway enforces what that identity is allowed to do at runtime. On VCF with VMware vSphere Kubernetes Service (VKS), both run entirely on the customer’s infrastructure. There is no external cloud dependency and no third-party governance plane. Nothing leaves the corporate perimeter.

What the Combined Solution Delivers

  • One endpoint for every model. A single standard API routes requests across on-premises models and cloud providers such as Gemini, OpenAI, and Anthropic. Routing follows the model named in the request, so teams add, switch, or retire a provider without touching client code.
  • Cost visible and enforced at the source. Every request captures prompt and completion token counts and exports them over OpenTelemetry to the Solo Enterprise dashboard, broken down by model, route, and team. Token budgets apply gateway-wide and per consumer, enforced before the upstream model is contacted. A spent budget rejects the request outright, consuming no tokens and incurring no provider charge.
  • Agents with bounded permissions. kagent assigns each agent an identity and declared scope; agentgateway enforces per-tool MCP policies and A2A rules at runtime. An agent granted read access to a tool cannot write to it, and communication between agents follows deny-by-default policy. Both are logged.
  • Lifecycle managed like any other workload. Agents are declared, deployed, updated, and removed through Kubernetes resources tied into VCF’s identity and RBAC. The full chain, from agent to tool call, is auditable, and built-in agents cover common platform operations out of the box.
  • A complete on-premises record. Traces, token metrics, tool calls, and policy decisions are stored and queryable inside VCF, giving security and compliance teams the same visibility over agents that they hold over any production service.

Why VCF and Solo.io?

VCF is the established platform for enterprise private cloud, with the compute, storage, and networking consistency that large organizations run production workloads on. Solo.io adds the layer that makes agents ready for that platform: managed identity and lifecycle from kagent, and traffic governance, cost control, and audit from agentgateway.

The result is coherent rather than bolted together. Agents get identity and permissions on the same infrastructure that already runs the enterprise’s critical services, governed by the workflows and controls teams use today. Organizations gain a path to production AI that their security, compliance, and finance functions can sign off on.

The key capabilities validated are: multi-LLM routing across on-premises and cloud backends, token attribution and rate limiting, MCP per-tool scope enforcement, A2A governance, and kagent CRD-based agent lifecycle management. A joint technical reference architecture and deployment guide are in development.

Business Benefits

Agents become governed infrastructure, not ungoverned processes. kagent brings agents under managed identity and lifecycle; agentgateway scopes and logs every action they take. The two close the governance gap end to end — identity, permission, and audit — so security teams can approve agent deployments on the same terms as any other workload.

AI stays inside the perimeter. Agent runtime, traffic governance, policies, and audit logs all run within VCF. No sensitive data or telemetry is sent to an external service. For financial services, healthcare, and government, this is what makes production AI viable rather than a pilot.

Inference cost is controlled before it is incurred. Usage is attributed to the team, project, or key that generated it and capped at the gateway before a provider bills for it. Platform teams produce accurate charge backs and enforce per-team limits without reconciling cloud invoices after the fact.

No new operating model. The stack does not introduce a separate management plane or a new discipline for operators. Agents run as workloads inside VCF, under the same access controls, observability pipelines, and change management already in place. Solo.io reports the gateway delivers markedly lower latency and higher throughput than legacy proxies, so the added governance does not come at the cost of performance.

item.content:encoded:
Join us at Explore

Las Vegas, Nevada | The Venetian

Aug. 31 – Sep. 3, 2026

REGISTER NOW

Mastering private cloud infrastructure takes a lot of technical skill, but it also takes a solid support system. You can read all the documentation in the world, but nothing beats asking a peer, “How did you actually get this to work without breaking production?”

At VMware Explore 2026 in Las Vegas, we want you to build connections that matter. If you already read our previous blog on Four Key Benefits of Attending, you know we are serious about training, but we are equally serious about community. Tap into a community powerhouse from Aug. 31 to Sep. 3 at the Venetian Convention and Expo Center. Here’s a quick reference guide to inform your journey…

Heading to #VMwareExplore this year? From the Communities Lounge to the VMware {code} Hackathon, this is your handy guide to all the community happenings in Las Vegas.
Share on X

The Communities Lounge and Meet-ups

Visit the Communities Lounge in The Hub to connect with fellow community members, leaders, or to relax between sessions. This space includes dedicated areas for all community groups to meet new members and catch up with old friends.

During the week, the Communities Lounge will host the following gatherings:

  • vExperts Meet-up, open to all current vExperts: Monday, Aug. 31 | 11:00 AM – 12:00 PM PDT
  • AMA with Community Experts, William Lam and Duncan Epping, open to all: Monday, Aug. 31 | 2:00 – 3:00 PM PDT
  • Homelab Meet-up, open to all: Tuesday, Sep. 1 | 10:00 – 11:00 AM PDT
  • Explore Insiders Meet-up, open to all: Tuesday, Sep.1 | 4:00 – 4:45 PM PDT
  • VMware {code} Sensor Meet-up, open to all: Wednesday, Sep. 3 | 11:00 AM – 12:00 PM PDT

The Hub Theater: Quick Talk Sessions

Hear what’s top of mind from community experts at the Hub Theater. This year, there are more than 40 Quick Talk sessions ranging from private cloud, AI, certifications, and more.

QUICK TALKS FULL SCHEDULE

VMware User Group (VMUG)

Officially launched in August of 2010, VMUG is an independent, global, customer-led organization, created to empower technologists through knowledge sharing, training, collaboration, and events focused on maximizing their use of VMware Cloud Foundation and the broader technologies needed in their ever-evolving role. For more than a decade, VMUG has been committed to creating space for IT practitioners, experts, and leaders to come together to solve complex virtualization problems. VMUG proves that progress is powered by community. 

At VMware Explore in Las Vegas, engage with VMUG in the following ways: 

  • Visit VMUG at Booth #205 to participate in our spin-the-wheel activation and win fantastic prizes such as:
    • Advantage Members Giveaway: Lenovo P5 ThinkStation Homelab gifted by Intel
    • All Member Giveaway: Nintendo Switch 2 Bundle
  • Join Brad Tompkins on Wednesday, September from 3:00 – 3:20 PM PDT for the VMUG quick talk session, Real Talk: What the VMUG Community Is Seeing in the VMware Ecosystem.
  • The VMUG Member Reception will take place at Wakuda on Tuesday, September 1 from 5:30 – 7:30 PM PDT, featuring drinks, appetizers, and a great time! RSVP here and save your spot.

VMware {code}: For the Developers and Automation Enthusiasts

VMware {code} is a vibrant community of developers and IT professionals who are passionate about driving technology forward. The community is for participants to explore cutting-edge technology and tools, connect with experts and peers to share knowledge, and innovate by collaborating on projects that shape the future of computing.

Home Lab Meetup | Tuesday, Sep. 1 | 10:00 – 11:00 AM PDT
Swap ideas with the Home Lab community, explore the latest mini workstations and PCs, and discover smart strategies for VCF 9.1 memory expansion. We will cover extending memory footprints on legacy hardware and getting your VMUG Advantage Home Lab licenses.

VMware {code} Lab Sensor Meetup | Wednesday, Sep. 2 | 10:00 – 11:00 AM PDT
Want to deploy Raspberry Pi sensors as Kubernetes workloads? Stop by to pick up a free sensor, dive into the code on VMware vSphere® Kubernetes Service (VKS), and collaborate on your favorite projects with the community. Open to all. Sensors given on a first-come, first-served basis.   

VMware {code} Hackathon

Monday, August 31 | 7:00 – 11:00 PM PDT | Level 2, Titian 2206

The VMware {code} Hackathon returns to VMware Explore in Las Vegas 2026—but this year we’re doing something different. Artificial Intelligence is transforming how we design, build, and automate software. Rather than a traditional coding competition, we’re inviting the VMware {code} Community to explore what happens when people and AI create together. 

Teams will be challenged to build a start-to-finish working prototype using AI as a core part of development over the course of one single evening. Join a team, or form a new one, onsite at the Hackathon.

Full event schedule:

  • 7:00 – 7:30 PM: Interactive AI Build Lab & Team Formation
  • 7:30 PM: Hackathon Begins
  • 10:30 PM: Team Presentations
  • 11:00 PM: Awards
  • 11:30 PM: Event ends
LEARN MORE AND SIGN UP FOR THE HACKATHON

The vExperts program awards individuals for their contributions to the VMware software ecosystem. Earning the award means a demonstrated strong commitment to sharing knowledge and recognition from peers for community contributions. There are many advantages to becoming a vExpert, including being instantly connected to a vast network of over 1,000 members. Get to know the vExpert program while at Explore.

vExpert Meetup at Explore

Monday, August 31 | 11:00 AM – 12 PM PDT | The Hub, Communities Lounge

At VMware Explore in Las Vegas, attending vExperts will kick off the busy week at the Communities Lounge inside of the Hub on day one, August 31 from 11:00 AM to 12:00 PM PDT. Get to know Eric Nielsen, Community Program Manager, and fellow certified vExperts for an hour of networking, community building, and fun. 

If you’re not already a vExpert, come by the Communities Lounge at any time to learn how to become one!

Broadcom Rewards Program

Program members earn points for completing online, in-platform activities, including education challenges, surveys, feedback forums, social shares, and more. Eligible members can redeem points for prizes in the Rewards catalog ranging from charity donations and certification vouchers to branded swag and high-tech gadgets!
